summary.intent: Execute Phase 21 gap closure plans (4 plans: SDK pinning wiring, TEE connection test, Pinata provider, BYO benchmarks), then run code review and security audit on the resulting changes.
summary.outcome: All 4 gap closure plans executed and verified. Simplify pass fixed a type bug, 3 deduplication issues, 4 efficiency issues, and comment cleanup. Security audit found and fixed 2 high-severity SSRF issues (blocklist gaps + DNS rebinding TOCTOU) plus a batch size limit. Changes were not committed during simplify/security phases and required a manual commit at the end.

repo: ByoIpfsConfig.protocol in packages/core/src/vault/types.ts was missing 'pinata' — it only had 'psa' | 'kubo', causing type mismatch with ExternalProviderConfig in sdk-core which added 'pinata'
The BYO IPNS localStorage key 'cipherbox-byo-ipns-name' was defined as a constant BYO_IPNS_NAME_KEY in StorageTab.tsx but used as a bare magic string in useAuth.ts
checkQuota() in vault.service.ts had a redundant isUserByo() DB query — it called isUserByo() then called getQuota() which also called isUserByo() internally
migration.service.ts loaded all PinnedCid rows via .find() just to get the count — should use .count()
StorageQuota.tsx had a local formatBytes() function duplicating the existing one in apps/web/src/utils/format.ts
ssrf-validation.ts had copy-pasted private IP range checks in both validateEndpointUrl and validateResolvedIp — missing 0.0.0.0, ::ffff IPv4-mapped IPv6, and 100.64.0.0/10 CGN range
TEE worker used bare fetch() calls throughout connection-test and migration-worker, making them vulnerable to redirect-based SSRF bypass
authTokenString() in migration-worker was called per-CID (up to 3x per CID) instead of once per batch
MigrationProgress.tsx polled unconditionally even when no migration existed, and called setMigration on every poll regardless of whether state changed
The phase 21 execution ran on a worktree at /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box-phase-20 while the main repo is at /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box

code.finding: protocol field was 'psa' | 'kubo' — missing 'pinata' variant added in Phase 21
Duplicate private IP range check logic in validateEndpointUrl and validateResolvedIp — extracted to isPrivateAddress() helper; also missing 0.0.0.0, CGN range, IPv4-mapped IPv6
Added ssrfSafeFetch() wrapper with redirect:'error' to prevent redirect-based SSRF bypass; all TEE worker fetch() calls now use this
checkQuota() called isUserByo() then getQuota() which called isUserByo() again — 2 DB round-trips per non-BYO upload on the hot path
Used .find() to load all PinnedCid entities just to get count — replaced with .count()
authTokenString() decoded per-CID (3x per CID), now decoded once per batch; fetch() replaced with ssrfSafeFetch()
Polling interval started unconditionally on mount even with no migration; setMigration fired on every poll regardless of value changes
11 numbered step comments removed from handleSave — they narrated obvious code; also step 9b broke the numbering scheme

workflow: GSD executor agents complete in ~5-9 minutes per plan, using 80-116k tokens each
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code bug can be detected by checking SUMMARY.md existence and git commits as a success proxy
Simplify and security:review should commit their changes incrementally — doing all edits then committing at the end risks losing context about which changes belong together
Pinata JWTs must start with 'eyJ' — an accidental leading 'b' was caught by curl auth verification
Security test files for TEE worker SSRF require careful mocking — dns.lookup module mocking has ESM limitations requiring workarounds
git pull with divergent branches needs explicit --rebase or --no-rebase; unstaged changes must be committed or stashed first

friction: GitHub connectivity was intermittent — git fetch timed out on first attempt, requiring retry
Simplify and security:review fixes were not committed during the session, leaving unstaged changes that blocked git pull --rebase
The user had to manually export env vars for Pinata configuration; the JWT had a leading 'b' typo that required a second export
ESM module mocking limitations in the TEE worker test environment required test restructuring for SSRF validation tests
ROADMAP.md had incorrect gap closure plan checkboxes and broken progress table columns that weren't caught by the phase completion tooling
